Representative timings and memory measurements for GACT/gsuite workflows, with an official MAGMA comparison for gene and classical pathway analyses. The benchmarks use CAD/T2D summary data and simulated workloads; they do not reproduce the original UK Biobank manuscript analyses.

## At a glance

Times below refer to the boundaries named in each row. Preparation, fitting, process and whole-call clocks are different measurements; component clocks are not additional costs to add to an inclusive total.

| Workflow | Measured workload | Preparation (s) | Analysis or call (s) | Reported peak memory |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Database setup | 2.57 GiB transferred; 3.04 GiB retained | Included | 544.20 download/setup | 2.68 GiB |
| Gene analysis: VEGAS | Two traits; 17,862 genes; 503 EUR reference people | 643.36 spectra + 79.52 conversion | 97.69 initial gene call; **899.94 inclusive analysis** | 5.88 GiB, whole worker |
| Classical pathways | 1,324 pathways per trait | 32.691 / 31.123 | 0.0226 / 0.0195 fitting; 50.299 / 32.395 process | Not recorded |
| Bayesian pathways | 17,955 gene scores; 1,324 sets | 1.33 single / 37.81 joint | 4.75 / 30.99 BLR; 6.07 / 68.86 whole call | 0.16 / 0.52 GiB, whole worker |
| PoPS: one full-data model | 17,955 gene scores; 1,324 sets | 1.02 BayesC / 1.81 BayesR | 6.77 / 84.88 BLR; 7.82 / 86.72 whole call | 0.15 GiB, whole worker |
| Fine-mapping | 5,000 simulated people; 37,991 markers | Prepared LD supplied | 2.36 genome fit; 5.48 four regional fits | 0.81 / 0.56 GiB, median process peak |
| Score application | 2,000 simulated recipients; 50,000 available SNPs | Excluded | 13.67 / 3.78 total-score application, 1 / 4 threads | 156.2 / 155.7 MiB, whole worker |

The fine-mapping summary gives medians of three one-chain runs; two-chain measurements are listed below. Scoring refers to a cell in the controlled grid. The detailed sections specify controls and clock boundaries for each workload. PoPS chromosome-held-out validation is reported separately from single-model fits.

## Gene analysis: VEGAS and MAGMA

Both result collections contain **17,862 genes per trait** with matching gene IDs and zero per-gene SNP-count mismatches. The MAGMA comparison uses **3,192,403 SNPs** and a **503-person EUR reference**.

### Timings

| Trait scope / operation | gsuite VEGAS analysis clock (s) | Official MAGMA gene-process clock (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GWAS1 initial analysis | Not timed separately | 4333.469 |
| GWAS2 initial analysis | Not timed separately | 4029.865 |
| Both traits: initial analysis | **899.94**, shared preparation and initial gene analysis | **8363.334**, sum of the two processes above |
| Both traits: alternative prepared refit | **71.44**, prepared-object loading excluded | Not timed |

VEGAS shares regional preparation across the two traits. Its **899.94-second analysis clock** includes spectra, prepared-object conversion, alignment, the initial gene call and checkpoint/cleanup overhead. Recorded components are **643.36 s** for spectra, **79.52 s** for conversion and **97.69 s** for the initial two-trait gene call. These are included in the analysis total. File loading (**110.45 s**) and neighbouring-gene correlation preparation are excluded. Peak whole-worker memory is **5.88 GiB**, including loading. Preparation uses four decoding threads; regional products/eigensolvers are serial.

The **71.44-second prepared refit** is an alternative reuse measurement, excluding **17.26 s** for prepared-object loading. Per-trait VEGAS times were not recorded. MAGMA's gene-process clocks include startup, loading, gene analysis, neighbouring-gene correlation work and output. **These timing boundaries differ**, so the table does not give an identical-work speedup. Gene and pathway clocks come from separate runs, not a measured end-to-end pipeline.

<span id="gene-result-agreement-from-saved-outputs"></span>

### Agreement

The gene results show **strong overall agreement**, with rank correlations of approximately **0.999 in both traits**. All 17,862 p-value pairs per trait are finite and positive; comparisons align genes by ID.

| Trait | Gene p-value pairs | Spearman of -log10(p) | Median absolute p difference | Maximum absolute p difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GWAS1 | 17,862 | 0.998947 | 0.003551 | 0.197081 |
| GWAS2 | 17,862 | 0.998791 | 0.004088 | 0.227723 |

At the descriptive Bonferroni threshold **0.05/17,862 = 2.79924e-6**:

| Trait | MAGMA significant | gsuite significant | Significant in both |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GWAS1 | 181 | 166 | 166 |
| GWAS2 | 40 | 38 | 38 |

**Every gsuite-significant gene is also significant in MAGMA.** MAGMA has **15 and 2 additional significant genes**, respectively. Some discordant calls involve substantial p-value differences rather than marginal threshold crossings.

Median absolute log10(p) differences are **0.00764 and 0.00623**; maxima are **19.931 and 2.975**. Extreme-tail differences can alter the reported strength of evidence while leaving a gene significant in both methods. This is strong overall concordance, not exact numerical equivalence or a calibration assessment.

<details><summary>Gene-tail methods and parameter counts</summary>

The saved gsuite results use saddlepoint evaluation with **1 and 2 moment-matched chi-square fallbacks**. None of the 17 additional MAGMA significance calls used that fallback. MAGMA uses its standard integration/simulation route. The reported gsuite `effective_parameters` and MAGMA `NPARAM` fields differ for **4,505 genes per trait**; tail evaluation alone has not been established as the explanation for every discrepancy.

</details>

**Evidence:** [VEGAS workload and methods](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/manuscript-vegas-complete-20261005/README.md), [component clocks](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/manuscript-vegas-complete-20261005/phase-summary.csv), [gene-agreement summary](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/gene-agreement-summary.json), [aggregate table](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/gene-agreement-summary.csv), [read-only comparison code](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/compare_saved_gene_results.py).

## Pathway analysis

<span id="classical-gsuite-pathway-fits-and-official-magma-comparison"></span>

### Classical gsuite and official MAGMA

The classical comparison uses **17,862 saved genes and 1,324 Reactome pathways per trait**, with **the same saved MAGMA gene statistics, gene properties and gene correlations** in both implementations. Gene-statistic computation is an upstream stage, excluded from these gsuite pathway clocks.

| Trait | gsuite preparation (s) | gsuite fitting (s) | gsuite process wall (s) | MAGMA gene-set process wall (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GWAS1 | 32.691 | 0.0226 | 50.299 | 29.451 |
| GWAS2 | 31.123 | 0.0195 | 32.395 | 79.332 |

Preparation maps sets, transforms gene responses/properties, prepares powered regional correlation inverses, adjusts covariates and caches shared/set cross-products. Fitting uses these summaries for the pathway regressions. Each trait ran in a separate process, with preparation measured separately.

**Timing boundaries:** gsuite measurements are native C++ gsea/gsolve Release/MKL with a one-thread limit; R interface conversion is excluded. Input loading takes **0.849 / 0.850 s**, separately. Process totals include startup, output and cleanup. **16.736 / 0.403 s** lies outside the internal loading/preparation/fitting clocks and remains included in the process totals. Peak memory was not recorded. MAGMA 1.10 gene-set process clocks include loading, correlation preparation, regression and output; separate preparation/fitting clocks were not recorded. Compare process clocks with process clocks, not with gsuite fitting alone.

| Trait | Maximum absolute beta difference | Maximum absolute SE difference | Maximum absolute p difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GWAS1 | 3.731e-05 | 4.994e-06 | 5.003e-06 |
| GWAS2 | 3.806e-05 | 4.997e-06 | 5.005e-06 |

**All 2,648 pathway fits meet the 2e-4 absolute beta/SE/p tolerance** against rounded MAGMA text outputs. P-value Spearman agreement exceeds **0.99999998** in both traits, with matching gene backgrounds/pathway IDs and zero pathway-size mismatches. This agreement concerns the **classical model on shared MAGMA gene inputs**, distinct from the VEGAS/MAGMA gene comparison and the Bayesian models.

<details><summary>Classical model settings</summary>

Correlation power is **1.1**, with an absolute eigenvalue cutoff of **0.1**, retained rank **13,814** and residual degrees of freedom **13,812**. All genes remain in the background; pruning removes correlation directions. Preparation uses **33 shared block applications** and **223,548 within-set precision entries**. Each trait has one recorded execution.

</details>

**Evidence:** [comparison report and provenance](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/README.md), [exact timings](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/measurements.csv), [agreement checks](../benchmarks/results/20261020-classical-magma-comparison/agreement.json).

### Bayesian gene-set analysis

Bayesian models use **17,955 saved gene scores and 1,324 Reactome sets** from hsa.0.0.1, with gsea **0.1.2** and gbayes **0.1.6**. Gene-statistic computation and cached input loading precede the measured calls. This gene collection differs from the classical comparison above.

| Full-data model | Preparation (s) | BLR fit (s) | Whole call (s) | Process peak (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bayesian MAGMA: single-trait BayesC | 1.33 | 4.75 | 6.07 | 0.16 |
| Bayesian MAGMA: joint GWAS1/GWAS2 BayesC | 37.81 | 30.99 | 68.86 | 0.52 |

Each model uses two chains, seeds 10/11 and one requested thread. Single-trait BayesC uses pi=.01, **5,000 sampling + 1,000 burn-in sweeps**; joint BayesC uses **1,000 + 200**. Hyperparameters are fixed at the model defaults.

Preparation includes validation, set mapping and model summaries. Single-trait independent-gene models form cross-products directly from sets; the joint model uses projected preparation. BLR clocks include validation, sampling, posterior accumulation and coefficient back-transformation. Whole-call clocks also include posterior summaries/prediction and interface overhead, excluding startup and serialization. Memory is whole-worker lifetime peak, including loading and saving, not per-phase memory. These timings do not establish MCMC convergence.

**Evidence:** [settings, phase timings, memory and input/code hashes](../benchmarks/results/20261019-direct-cross-products/README.md).

## PoPS gene prioritization

### Single full-data fit

These fits use the same **17,955 saved gene scores and 1,324 Reactome sets**, gsea 0.1.2/gbayes 0.1.6 and timing boundaries described for Bayesian pathways. Upstream gene-statistic computation is excluded.

| Full-data model | Preparation (s) | BLR fit (s) | Whole call (s) | Process peak (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PoPS: one full-data BayesC model | 1.02 | 6.77 | 7.82 | 0.15 |
| PoPS: one full-data BayesR model | 1.81 | 84.88 | 86.72 | 0.15 |

Both use two chains, seeds 10/11, one requested thread, pi=.001 and **5,000 sampling + 1,000 burn-in sweeps**. PoPS learns slab variance, residual variance and mixture weights; BayesR divides the initial active probability among three components. Intercept-only pathway residual normalization is n-1. BLR fitting uses direct sufficient statistics through native gbayes; the R interface is `gsea::blr()`.

<span id="separate-22-fold-chromosome-held-out-validation"></span>

### Chromosome-held-out validation

| Validation workflow | Preparation (s) | Sum of BLR fits (s) | Prediction (s) | Whole call (s) | Process peak (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PoPS BayesC: 22 held-out chromosome folds | 33.64 | 156.90 | 1.27 | 192.97 | 0.24 |
| PoPS BayesR: 22 held-out chromosome folds | 35.82 | 1555.23 | 1.30 | 1593.50 | 0.26 |

Each validation workflow fits **22 training models**, each with two chains and **5,000 sampling + 1,000 burn-in sweeps**. Saved gene scores are reused; preparation uses training genes only. BLR time is summed across folds and held-out prediction is timed separately. These validation costs are separate from a single full-data fit. Each setting has one execution, without a repeated-run variability estimate. Memory is whole-worker peak; the 1,536 MiB preparation guard is a matrix-payload limit, not measured memory.

**Evidence:** [full-data and per-fold phase records, settings and hashes](../benchmarks/results/20261019-direct-cross-products/README.md).

## Association and fine-mapping

The simulated panel has **5,000 people and 37,991 filtered markers**. Fit times exclude download, simulation, QC, startup and whole-genome sparse-LD preparation.

| Operation | Threads | Wall time | Process peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear regression | 4 | 1.64 s | 153 MiB |
| Gaussian LOCO | 4 | 57.00 s | 386 MiB |
| Prior-selected LOCO | 4 | 124.12 s | 392 MiB |
| Four regional BayesC fits and posterior sets | 1 | 5.48 s (5.22–6.28) | 0.56 GiB |
| Genome-wide BayesC fit from prepared LD | 1 | 2.36 s (2.03–2.38) | 0.81 GiB |
| Genome-wide credible-set grouping | 1 | 3.95 s (3.83–4.16) | 0.52 GiB |

Association rows are single runs. Fine-mapping rows give medians and ranges of three serial repeats; memory is median whole-process peak. Regional BayesC uses one chain, **1,000 sampling + 100 burn-in sweeps** across four regions with **850, 785, 1,091 and 1,399 markers**. The genome fit uses one chain and **100 sweeps without burn-in**. These controls measure computational cost, not convergence or calibrated inference.

### Two-chain and chromosome-component workloads

| Operation | Status | Seconds | Process peak GiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chromosome-component Gaussian LOCO | completed | 90.26 | 0.35 |
| Chromosome-component prior-selected LOCO | completed | 67.07 | 0.37 |
| Two-chain genome-wide BayesC from cached LD | completed | 2.91 | 0.67 |
| Two-chain regional BayesC | completed | 6.13 | 0.34 |

**Evidence:** [fine-mapping controls and measurements](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/manuscript-simulated-finemapping-dense-20261006/README.md), [two-chain and chromosome-component records](../benchmarks/results/20261019-gsuite-revision/README.md).

## Polygenic score application

The **40-cell controlled scoring grid** uses gbase 0.1.3/gscore 0.1.1 with frozen gsim-derived effects and artificial-LD genotypes. It varies **500 / 2,000 recipients**, **10,000 / 50,000 available SNPs**, **0 / 3 / 20 sets**, adjacent-set overlap **0 / 0.5**, and **1 / 4 requested threads**. Each synthetic set has 500 SNPs; available SNPs and the union contributing to set scores are different quantities.

| Example workload | Seconds: 1 / 4 threads | Process MiB: 1 / 4 threads |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total score: 2,000 recipients, 50,000 SNPs | 13.67 / 3.78 | 156.2 / 155.7 |
| 20 sets, no overlap: 2,000 recipients, 50,000 available SNPs; 10,000 union SNPs | 4.75 / 1.35 | 159.0 / 166.4 |
| 20 sets, 50% adjacent overlap: same recipients/available SNPs; 5,250 union SNPs | 2.39 / 0.73 | 159.2 / 159.7 |

Score-application clocks exclude preparation and loading; memory covers the whole R worker including serialization. Weights are fixed, genotype coding standardized and completed scores unscaled. Each cell is one execution: this measures bounded workload sensitivity, not prediction accuracy or a general scaling law. These scoring benchmarks use simulated recipients, not UK Biobank.

### Reference-derived simulation

A gsim reference-conditioned chr22 panel from **503 EUR donors** retains **5,360 SNPs**, with **2,000 recipients** and three synthetic pathway sets. With one requested thread, total scoring takes **1.03 s / 157.2 MiB** and three-pathway scoring **2.41 s / 157.8 MiB**. Effects are fixed simulated weights. Operation clocks exclude preparation, loading and serialization; memory includes loading/saving. Each setting is one execution. This is a separate workload from the controlled grid.

**Evidence:** [full scoring grid and measurement definitions](Benchmark_scoring_details.html), [reference-derived measurements](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/20261004-real-1000g/measurements.csv), [grid scripts and records](../benchmarks/results/20261019-gsuite-revision/README.md).

## Database setup and genetic correlation

| Operation | Threads | Wall time | Resident memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Database download and setup | 1 requested | 544.20 s | 2.68 GiB |
| VEGAS complete initial analysis | 4 decoding; serial spectra | 899.94 s | 5.88 GiB |
| LDSC | No fitter thread argument | 9.28 s | 3.02 GiB |
| GNOVA | No fitter thread argument | 6.39 s | 3.09 GiB |
| SumHer equal-marker baseline | No fitter thread argument | 12.87 s | 3.53 GiB |
| Chromosome-set LDSC preparation and fit | No fitter thread argument | 29.91 s | 3.27 GiB |
| HESS regional preparation | 4 | 1128.67 s | 3.18 GiB |
| HESS raw pair refit | No fitter thread argument | 3.61 s | 0.41 GiB |
| HESS partial pair refit | No fitter thread argument | 3.31 s | 0.43 GiB |

Database setup transfers **2.57 GiB** and retains **3.04 GiB** locally: 2.63 GiB non-ZIP files and a 0.41 GiB ZIP archive, excluding the separate genotype reference and serialized descriptor. The clock measures download/setup, excluding package installation, and depends on network conditions. Versions are recorded with the source evidence. VEGAS scope and timing boundaries are given in the gene-analysis section.

Correlation fits use **7,221,923 common marker rows**. Memory is a sampled analysis peak with inputs loaded before the clock. HESS prepares **1,702 regions and 18,696 components**; refits reuse compact moments. SumHer is an equal-marker baseline. Estimator assumptions are described in the [correlation tutorial](Genetic_correlation_CAD_T2D_gcorr.html).

**Evidence:** [database and tutorial measurement records](../benchmarks/scripts/website-snapshot/Tutorial_timings_and_memory.Rmd), [correlation timing and memory](../benchmarks/results/website-data/gcorr-current-timings-memory.csv).

## Measurement definitions and reproducibility

Measurements were recorded on an **Intel Core i7-1365U**, approximately **16 GiB RAM**, **Windows / R 4.4.1**. Exact software versions and execution dates belong to each linked evidence collection; the page combines measured workloads from multiple software snapshots.

- **Preparation** covers the input validation, mapping and reusable summaries specified for that workflow.
- **Fitting / analysis** covers the named computational call; loading and preparation are included only where stated.
- **Whole-call** includes interface and result-assembly costs, but excludes process startup/serialization where specified.
- **Process wall time** includes worker startup, loading, computation and output.
- **Memory** is resident working set, not result size or incremental solver allocation. Whole-worker peaks and sampled analysis peaks are labeled separately. Per-phase VEGAS/BLR memory and classical comparison peak memory were not recorded.
- **Threads** are requested limits, not observed worker counts. Single-run timings do not provide repeated-run uncertainty; three-repeat summaries are explicitly labeled.

The [consolidated evidence table](../benchmarks/revision/consolidated-timings.md) retains exact clocks, qualifications and source references. [Source locations/checksums](../benchmarks/provenance.csv), [selected-record hashes](../benchmarks/revision/consolidated-sources.json) and the [benchmark script collection](../benchmarks/README.md) support reproducibility. The linked records retain full provenance; databases, raw fits, gene-level outputs and executables are excluded from the website evidence collection.
